finding: open_confined_fallback has NO anchor guard, so the exact attack TEST-14 documents succeeds on every non-Linux host and on Linux <5.6 (the ENOSYS path). It computes root_canon = root.canonicalize() at read time; if the bundle root has been replaced by a symlink since resolve_conversation_workspace_dir() canonicalized it, BOTH canon and root_canon resolve under the attacker's target, starts_with() passes, and prompt_file: "etc/passwd" returns the host file. The Linux path defends this with O_NOFOLLOW|O_DIRECTORY on the anchor open; the fallback opens nothing anchored at all. The doc's justification ("acceptable because the untrusted writer runs on a Linux kernel on ALL THREE host platforms") is a non-sequitur: confinement is performed by the SERVER's kernel, not the sandbox guest's, and on macOS the workspace dir the guest can write to is a macOS host directory resolved by macOS. Proof that this is unguarded rather than merely undocumented: read_prompt_file_refuses_a_bundle_root_that_became_a_symlink (validate.rs:2330) is gated #[cfg(unix)], not #[cfg(target_os="linux")], so on macOS it does not guard the fallback - it FAILS it (the fixture's elsewhere/etc/passwd is a real regular file under the resolved root, so read_prompt_file returns Ok("HOST SECRET") where the test does expect_err).

how.flags sets O_NOFOLLOW, which in openat2 refuses the FINAL component if it is a symlink - including one that stays inside the bundle. That is the exact behaviour the comment three lines below claims the code avoids ("a symlink that stays inside the bundle still resolves, exactly as the non-Linux fallback allows... RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS is deliberately NOT set... so Linux and non-Linux would disagree about whether a bundle is valid"). Verified against the running kernel with the identical flags/resolve mask: prompts/link.md -> real.md returns ELOOP with O_NOFOLLOW in how.flags and an fd without it, while an intermediate in-bundle symlink (pdir/real.md) resolves either way. Consequences: (a) Linux and the fallback DO disagree, which is what the design set out to prevent; (b) the ELOOP is mapped to PromptFileError::Escape at line 1289, so a legitimate in-bundle symlink is reported to the author as the SECURITY finding WORKFLOW_PROMPT_FILE_ESCAPE with copy saying the file "ends up outside the workflow" - which is false. Reachable in practice on the run_from_workspace / validate_from_workspace surfaces, where the model authors the tree and can create symlinks (installed bundles cannot contain them - hub/bundle.rs rejects symlink entries).

validate_for_install_async was introduced for exactly this hazard but the untrusted-root callers were not converted. load_and_validate_workspace is an `async fn` that calls the SYNC validate_for_install(&def, root, false) where root is the conversation's code_sandbox workspace - the one bundle root an untrusted model writes to. Since this diff, validate_collecting READS every prompt_file (up to MAX_PROMPT_FILE_BYTES each) with std::fs, so a tokio worker is parked for the whole read set on a model-triggerable MCP verb. validate_from_workspace (tools.rs:683) has the same shape with validate_collecting. The doc on validate_for_install_async (validate.rs:579-582) asserts "The draft-validation handlers pass a non-existent bundle root and so read nothing, but spawn_run/resume_run pass the extracted bundle" - that enumeration is wrong; these two plus hub/handlers.rs:2187, workflow/handlers/dev.rs:268 and :564 all pass a real bundle root from an async fn.

Work-amplification DoS newly introduced by making the validator READ every prompt_file. validate_collecting runs check_prompt_files over ALL steps with no short-circuit on WORKFLOW_TOO_MANY_STEPS (check_steps_shape only PUSHES a finding at validate.rs:679; nothing returns early), and there is no memoisation of a repeated path. A model-authored workflow.yaml in its own sandbox workspace can therefore declare N steps (N bounded only by the size of the workflow.yaml the model writes, which is read with an uncapped tokio::fs::read_to_string) all pointing at ONE 1 MiB prompt file, and each validate_from_workspace / run_from_workspace call re-reads it N times - ~25 GB of reads for ~1 MB of YAML, executed synchronously on a tokio worker (see the unconverted-caller finding). Before this diff the same loop did one cheap canonicalize() per step.

openat2's EAGAIN is not handled. openat2(2) documents EAGAIN specifically for RESOLVE_BENEATH/RESOLVE_IN_ROOT when the kernel could not prove a '..' or symlink did not escape the root because of a racing rename, and states "the caller may wish to retry the operation". That is precisely the scenario this function was written for (a sandbox renaming directories under the bundle root while the resolution runs). It falls into the `_ =>` arm and becomes PromptFileError::Unreadable("Resource temporarily unavailable (os error 11)") -> WORKFLOW_PROMPT_FILE_MISSING, whose author-facing copy says the file "may be missing, be a folder rather than a file, be empty, be too large, or not be text" - none of which is true. A benign concurrent rename in the workspace thus fails a run with a misleading, unactionable verdict instead of retrying.

Only ENOSYS triggers open_confined_fallback, but a missing openat2 does not always surface as ENOSYS. A seccomp filter that does not list openat2 returns EPERM under Docker's default profile (openat2 was only added to moby's default seccomp profile in 20.10.10), and some sandboxed runtimes (gVisor/runsc, older qemu-user, restrictive systemd SystemCallFilter=) return EPERM or EINVAL. Any of those lands in the `_ =>` arm as PromptFileError::Unreadable, so EVERY prompt_file: in the deployment - installed bundles included - starts failing validate_for_install with WORKFLOW_PROMPT_FILE_MISSING and workflows that ran yesterday stop launching, with copy that blames the author's file. The fallback exists precisely to make "the kernel/runtime cannot do openat2" a deployment fact rather than an author error; the errno set it keys on is too narrow to deliver that.

read_prompt_file_refuses_a_bundle_root_that_became_a_symlink is gated #[cfg(unix)] although the behaviour it asserts exists only in the #[cfg(target_os = "linux")] openat2 branch. On macOS (a supported build/test host for this repo) open_confined is open_confined_fallback, which resolves the swapped root and returns Ok("HOST SECRET"), so the test's expect_err panics: the suite goes red on macOS rather than guarding anything. The same applies on any Linux kernel <5.6 via the ENOSYS path. Either gate it target_os="linux", or give the fallback the anchor guard it is asserting.

Silent behaviour change for already-installed data. spawn_run/resume_run re-validate against the real bundle, and read_prompt_file now hard-rejects four file states the previous existence-only check accepted: >1 MiB (TooLarge), non-UTF-8, zero-byte (Empty), and - via the widened check_prompt_file_shape - any path containing a backslash (a legal filename character on Linux, previously accepted and readable). A workflow installed before this change with any of those launches with WORKFLOW_PROMPT_FILE_MISSING and, on the resume_run path, an in-flight durable run becomes permanently unresumable. The intent is documented in the new code, but nothing in the diff migrates or even surveys existing rows, and the author-facing copy does not distinguish "your file is 1.2 MiB" from "your file is missing" beyond the free-form message.

ELOOP is folded into PromptFileError::Escape together with EXDEV, so three distinct causes - a RESOLVE_NO_MAGICLINKS rejection, an ordinary symlink loop / >40-link chain, and (per the O_NOFOLLOW finding) an ordinary in-bundle symlink - all report the security finding WORKFLOW_PROMPT_FILE_ESCAPE, whose copy states the file "ends up outside the workflow once the location is followed". Only EXDEV actually means that. The comment acknowledges the conflation but the author-facing consequence (a false security verdict on a file that is inside the bundle) is not sound.

Same unconverted-caller class as the workflow_mcp verbs, but this one blocks a tokio worker while holding the per-workflow update lock: validate::validate_for_install(&def, &bundle_root, true) is called from an async fn inside the locked section, and since this diff that call performs the full prompt_file read set. hub/handlers.rs:2187 and dev.rs:268 are the same shape without the lock. All four should use validate_for_install_async.

The controlClearanceDelta invariant (`delta >= 0` is a failure) is unsatisfiable for any InputGroup carrying BOTH an inline-start and an inline-end addon. The group root applies has-[>[data-align=inline-end]]:[&>input]:pe-1.5 AND has-[>[data-align=inline-start]]:[&>input]:ps-1.5, so both sides of the control are tightened to 6px and the delta is exactly 0 for both probe rows. No such consumer exists in the gallery today (the spec's own "what this does not cover" note names adjacent gaps but not this one), so the spec passes for now and turns red the first time a two-addon group is added - failing on the correct component for the wrong reason.

REJECTED: host filesystem path leaking into author-/model-visible text. Every PromptFileError string is built from either the author-supplied `rel` or a bare std::io::Error; Rust's std::fs errors (File::open, canonicalize, read) carry only the errno and never the path, and the `bundle root: {e}` prefix adds no path either. The findings surfaced to the model by workflow_mcp::validate_from_workspace and to the author by validate_for_install therefore expose no host path. (runner.rs's pre-existing `read workflow.yaml at {}` messages do leak the extracted path, but that is unchanged by this diff.)

REJECTED: unbounded allocation from a lying/large st_size. Vec::with_capacity is clamped with .min(MAX_PROMPT_FILE_BYTES) and the read goes through Read::take(MAX_PROMPT_FILE_BYTES + 1) with a post-read length re-check, so a single read_prompt_file cannot allocate more than ~1 MiB regardless of what fstat reported or how the file grew. The real resource issue is the number of calls, not the size of one (see the amplification finding).

REJECTED: a FIFO or other blocking special file parking the thread. how.flags carries O_NONBLOCK (and so does the fallback's custom_flags), so open(2) on a FIFO with no writer returns immediately, and the type is then judged by fstat on the RETURNED fd (meta.is_file()) rather than by a second path lookup - so neither a block nor a type-TOCTOU is available here. TEST-12 pins the FIFO case with a real mkfifo.

REJECTED: unsound `?` on the nested Result in validate_for_install_async. spawn_blocking yields Result<Result<(), AppError>, JoinError>; the map_err converts the JoinError arm to AppError and `?` unwraps it, leaving the inner Result<(), AppError> as the function's tail expression. That is correct, and the WorkflowDef clone is a plain owned deep copy moved into the blocking closure with no borrow escaping.

REJECTED: check_prompt_file_shape panicking or being bypassed. `rel.as_bytes()[0]` is only reached inside `.get(1).is_some_and(...)`, which requires len >= 2, so no index panic; an embedded NUL is caught later by CString::new -> PromptFileError::Unsafe; and the empty string never reaches here because prompt_file_ref/prompt_source filter it out in both the validator and the runner. RESOLVE_BENEATH independently rejects absolute paths and '..' on the Linux path, so the shape check is defence in depth rather than the only guard.

REJECTED: fd leak or double-close around the openat2 result. The anchor `dir` File is owned for the whole syscall and dropped (closed) on every exit path; the returned raw fd is adopted exactly once by File::from_raw_fd and is dropped by every subsequent `?` in read_prompt_file. Nothing takes a second owner of either descriptor.

REJECTED: a step kind that bypasses the new confinement. All three prompt-carrying kinds funnel through load_raw_prompt - llm via resolve_prompt (dispatch.rs:187), llm_map directly (dispatch.rs:398), and agent via resolve_prompt (agent_dispatch.rs:1101). No remaining `extracted_path.join(prompt_file)` exists anywhere in the workflow module, and StepConfig::prompt_fields is an exhaustive match, so a future kind cannot be added silently.

REJECTED: the Layer A job narrowing from the whole visual testDir to gallery.config.json's visualSpecs is a coverage regression. The same commit adds `submodules: recursive`, without which `npm ci` cannot resolve the sdk/packages/* workspaces - so the previously-unfiltered invocation never reached Playwright at all and the effective gating set was empty. Curating up from zero is a net increase, and the un-gated specs are named explicitly in the workflow comment rather than dropped silently.
